Title: Ashfall Fossil Beds
Content: In `1971`, a paleontologist¹ made an important discovery in Nebraska. He found the fossil skeleton of a baby rhinoceros in a ravine. This discovery would have a large impact on science. Today, people can get a glimpse of this astounding discovery at Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park.

The region's climate was different `text(millions of years)` ago compared to the climate of today. Air temperatures were warmer, and the air was more humid. Due to the climate, the plants and animals that `ultext(inhabited)` the region were also different from those found there today. The climate, plants, and animals of Nebraska changed slowly over time. An `ultext(epic)` event that occurred long ago saved a record of the prehistoric era.

Many scientists believe that there was a tremendous volcanic eruption in the region `text(millions of years)` ago. The eruption released large amounts of ash into the atmosphere which spread into the air for `text(thousands of miles)` before falling back to `text(Earth)`. Animals inhaled the ash over a period of `text(weeks)` and died. The remains of the animals and geographic features became buried in a layer of volcanic matter. The skeletons of entire creatures were protected and preserved in this volcanic ash. Over the `text(years)`, they were fossilized.

Ashfall fossil beds are `text(one)` location where many fossil skeletons have been discovered. Fossils are common and have been found all over the world. Ashfall fossil beds, however, are `text(one)` of the few places where entire fossil skeletons have been found.

In `1991`, Ashfall Fossil Beds became a Nebraska state historical park. This was an important step in an effort to protect and preserve the fossil beds. Scientists can continue their study of the fossils without the threat of land development.

The park also offers visitors an opportunity to see what wildlife existed in the region `text(millions of years)` ago. It is a fascinating place where visitors can see fossilized remains of camels, giant turtles, saber-toothed deer, rhinoceros, and many other animals. The fact that there are so many complete, well-preserved fossils also makes the park an important scientific site.

Ashfall fossil beds are a unique phenomenon. The location continues to be studied, even `text(forty years)` after its discovery. More than `200` fossilized skeletons of `text(twelve)` prehistoric species have been uncovered. `text(Each fossil)` is carefully recorded and mapped in an effort to keep track of past and current finds. New discoveries are made `text(every year)`.

The Hubbard Rhino Barn is a large building that houses and protects areas being studied. It is named after the huge number of rhinoceros fossils discovered at the site. Students from the University of Nebraska gain field experience by working there.

Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park is located in northeastern Nebraska. The park covers `text(360 acres)` of rangeland in Antelope County. Visitors to the park can enjoy hiking and picnicking. Trails throughout the park provide many scenic views of the valley and a glimpse of the region's geological features. The trails also allow people to view the wildlife and plants that are present today in the region.

At the Rhino Barn, visitors can observe paleontologists at work. A goal of the facility is to spark wonder in children and adults. For anyone with an interest in prehistoric life, fossils, or paleontology, a trip to Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park would be time well spent.
